domain_label: Study System — Planner: Slice/Pass Decomposition & Specialist Sequencing (build-time orchestration)
purpose: A method for the FACTORY build planner to decompose one idea into numbered slices and single-beat passes over an explicit dependency DAG, and to sequence which design-authority specialist governs each slice and in what dependency order (schema->drawing->wording; data-producer->consumer), so that every slice is built by a loaded specialist inside its boundaries, against a composed acceptance test, with polish kept off the mainline critical path — a build/plan-time discipline strictly disjoint from sysloops' runtime self-improvement loops.
assumptions: no observed run of a planner-orchestrated build is supplied as a labeled dataset; every rule is grounded in the documented build history (PROTOCOL.md, SLICE_6_5.md, NEW_FEATURES_PLAN.md, BASE44_MASTER_PLAN.md) and tagged [FACT-source] where quoted, or [ESTIMATE] where it is design synthesis

the app's own code and the domain specialists (kgraph, viz, uxguide, contenteng, sched, learner, sysloops, ...) are the implementers/authorities; this KB sequences and verifies them, it does not re-derive their internals

'idempotent', 'loop', and 'router' are used here in their BUILD-TIME senses (duplicate-safe re-run of an import/build; the verification loop of a pass; sequencing which specialist governs a slice), never sysloops' runtime senses
the Slice 0->8 map is an EXEMPLAR of DAG shape, not a fixed template that transfers verbatim to a different idea
exclusions: the runtime nightly-analysis pipeline, self-metrics scorecard, FSRS re-fit gate, weakness diagnosis and degraded-mode (owned by sysloops; planner only sequences WHEN Slice 8 is built and verifies it was built as specified)
the actual app code of any slice (written by the build agent under the governing specialist's design authority)
the internal design method of each domain specialist (owned by that specialist; consumed here as the authority to load and obey)
the three-layer verification loop internals (kb2) and owner-gate design / continuous-mode discipline (kb3)
inventing any exam-blueprint number, endpoint, price or clinical fact

glossary.definition: a single-beat unit of build work with an explicit place in the dependency DAG; the next slice = the lowest-numbered slice not marked DONE, with the Slice-5 pull-forward exception [FACT-source: PROTOCOL step 1]

a sub-unit of a slice too large for one beat (e.g. Slice 6.5 Pass 1..4); the smallest schedulable build unit, each carrying the full per-unit treatment (specialists loaded, acceptance checks, ledger row, GitHub push) [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md]

the directed acyclic graph of hard dependencies among slices from which build order is derived; Slice 0 extracts prerequisites, Slice 1 is parallelizable, Slice 5 pulls forward after Slice 2, Slice 8 is last because it supervises earlier slices [FACT-source: BASE44_MASTER_PLAN slice map]

a decimal-numbered polish/beauty pass (Slice 6.5) placed off the mainline critical path so it NEVER blocks the next functional slice; owner-gated, mainline-wins-on-contention [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md]

the specialist JSON named in a slice's directive block that governs its design; loaded in full, obeyed by role+decision_procedure+boundaries, its validation_checklist forming part of the slice's acceptance test [FACT-source: PROTOCOL step 3]

the status of a slice built without loading its named specialist(s) in full; planner flags and halts it rather than accept design done from memory [FACT-source: PROTOCOL 'A slice built without loading its specialist(s) is out of contract']

ordering multiple specialists on one slice by what each consumes: schema/meaning before drawing before wording (kgraph->viz->uxguide, D1), and data-producer before data-consumer (category attribute before shape encoding, Feature B) [FACT-source: SLICE_6_5.md D1; NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §3B]

the union of the governing specialist(s)' validation_checklist and the slice's own acceptance checks, reported per item as PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED-BY-GATE [FACT-source: PROTOCOL step 3; SLICE_6_5 directive]

the 3-line statement preceding a build — which slice, which specialists loaded, which owner gates the slice ends with — kept terse because the repo ledger, not chat, is the record [FACT-source: PROTOCOL step 4]

one directive built in one pass with all its defects batched; a fix that fails twice is stopped and reported honestly rather than re-prompted a third time, because the re-prompt loop is the known credit sink [FACT-source: PROTOCOL credit discipline]

in planner's remit, a re-run of an import/build being duplicate-safe (a slice acceptance item verified by planner, designed by the owning specialist) — NOT sysloops' runtime sense of a nightly re-run reproducing the same DB state [FACT-source: NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §4 boundary]

nodes.definition: Frame the layer: planner owns BUILD/PLAN orchestration for a single-owner, specialist-governed app build — decompose an idea into ordered slices and single-beat passes, sequence which design-authority specialist governs each slice, run the three-layer verification loop, and design the owner gates. This KB is the DECOMPOSITION-AND-SEQUENCING third. The lifecycle is design/build-time (once per slice/pass), which is what separates planner from sysloops, whose subject is the running app improving ITSELF at runtime every night [FACT-source: NEW_FEATURES_PLAN §4 'planner = the build/plan orchestration. Different subject, different lifecycle']. planner plans and verifies the BUILD; it never writes the app's code and never approves a gate [ESTIMATE — design synthesis, high confidence].

nodes.definition: Decompose one idea into NUMBERED slices carrying an explicit dependency DAG: each slice states which earlier slices it hard-depends on, so ordering is derived from dependencies, not chosen by convenience. The worked example is the Slice 0→8 map [FACT-source: BASE44_MASTER_PLAN slice map]: Slice 0 extracts shared platform prerequisites; Slice 1 has zero hard deps and may run in parallel; Slice 5 may be pulled forward any time after Slice 2 (owner top priority); Slice 8 is last because it supervises everything earlier. The DAG is the artifact the whole build reads.

cons.claim: A DAG built on a wrong dependency claim orders the build wrong; dependency edges must be verified not assumed

conflict_axes.name: dependency_order_vs_convenience_order
conflict_axes.description: Ordering slices/specialists by the true dependency DAG can be slower to start than ordering by whatever is convenient, but convenience order forces rework when a hidden dependency surfaces.
poles: order by convenience / what looks ready
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: dependency order wins; a convenience order is only allowed where the DAG proves the slices are independent (e.g. Slice 1 parallel)

conflict_axes.name: load_in_full_vs_context_budget
conflict_axes.description: Loading several full specialist JSONs on a multi-domain slice costs context budget, tempting a partial read that risks crossing an unread boundary.
poles: load every governing specialist in full
read only the parts that seem relevant
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: load-in-full wins; a slice designed from a partial spec is out of contract

conflict_axes.name: polish_now_vs_mainline_first
conflict_axes.description: A rough surface tempts scheduling polish immediately, but polish on the mainline critical path blocks functional slices.
poles: schedule polish now on the mainline
keep polish as a background N.5 pass
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: mainline wins; polish is an N.5 pass that waits and yields on contention

conflict_axes.name: two_attempt_stop_vs_one_more_try
conflict_axes.description: A fix one tweak from working tempts a third attempt, but the third re-prompt is exactly the known credit sink.
poles: stop and report after two failed attempts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the two-attempt stop wins; report honestly and let the owner decide the next move

conflict_axes.name: planner_sequences_vs_planner_designs_slice8
conflict_axes.description: Sequencing and verifying Slice 8 puts planner close enough to its internals to be tempted to design them, which is sysloops' remit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: planner sequences and verifies; runtime-loop-internal design defers to sysloops

edge_cases.description: A dependency edge between two slices is assumed rather than verified, and turns out to be wrong (the true blocker is data, not rendering).
edge_cases.trigger: a slice is scheduled as independent but stalls on a missing input from an unscheduled slice
edge_cases.mitigation: verify each dependency edge before ordering; re-diagnose blocker as data vs rendering (Feature B lesson)

edge_cases.description: A slice touches a domain whose specialist was not named, so a whole facet (e.g. legend wording) ships ungoverned.
edge_cases.trigger: a slice's directive omits an authority for a domain it actually touches
edge_cases.mitigation: enumerate every domain the slice touches and name an authority for each before building

edge_cases.description: A slice is designed from a half-remembered specialist rather than a full load, crossing an unread boundary.
edge_cases.trigger: context-budget pressure prompts a partial read
edge_cases.mitigation: flag out-of-contract and halt; load in full before resuming

edge_cases.description: Multiple specialists on one slice run in arbitrary order, so a downstream authority reworks an upstream decision.
edge_cases.trigger: viz picks an encoding before kgraph fixes the datum
edge_cases.mitigation: order by consumption (schema->drawing->wording) before any of them designs

edge_cases.description: Later-slice work spotted mid-slice is built now, so the ledger row overstates what the beat did.
edge_cases.trigger: an obviously-cheap adjacent fix is folded in without authorization
edge_cases.mitigation: note-and-leave in the ledger; do not merge scope

edge_cases.description: A runtime-loop-internal question arrives inside a Slice 8 build and planner starts answering it.
edge_cases.trigger: a Slice 8 acceptance check turns on nightly self-metric thresholds
edge_cases.mitigation: defer the internal-design question to sysloops; planner verifies build-vs-spec only

workflow.action: Frame the build-time orchestration and set the sysloops fence
workflow.description: State the once-per-slice build lifecycle and the plan-not-implement posture before decomposing
workflow.gate: build-time-vs-runtime split and never-approve-a-gate posture stated

workflow.action: Decompose the idea into numbered slices with a dependency DAG
workflow.description: Produce numbered slices, each naming hard dependencies; mark parallel and pull-forward slices
workflow.gate: every slice names its hard dependencies; ordering is dependency-derived

workflow.action: Split oversized slices into single-beat passes
workflow.description: Break any slice too large for one beat into numbered passes, each a full unit; note-and-leave later-slice work
workflow.gate: one slice per beat; no skip, no scope-merge

workflow.action: Place polish as N.5 passes off the critical path
workflow.description: Number beauty/polish work as decimal slices that never block mainline
workflow.gate: polish cannot block a mainline slice; mainline wins on contention

workflow.action: Name and load the design authority per slice
workflow.description: Attach the governing specialist(s) to each slice and load them in full
workflow.gate: a slice without a loaded authority is out of contract

workflow.description: Sequence schema->drawing->wording and data-producer->consumer (D1, Feature B)
workflow.gate: no downstream authority runs before its upstream input is fixed

workflow.description: Union the specialist(s)' validation_checklist with the slice's own acceptance checks

workflow.action: Confirm before build, then build in one pass with a two-attempt stop
workflow.description: State the 3-line confirm (slice/specialists/gates); build once; stop a fix after two failed attempts
workflow.gate: the ledger is the record; a fix failing twice is stopped and reported

priority_rationale: The frame and the sysloops fence come first because every later decomposition and sequencing decision inherits the build-time-vs-runtime lifecycle and the plan-not-implement posture; if planner drifts into designing runtime loops the whole KB is mis-scoped. Decomposition (idea->slices->passes, no-skip/no-merge, N.5) precedes sequencing because you cannot name an authority for a slice that is not yet cut. Naming and loading the authority precedes ordering and acceptance because an unloaded or unnamed authority makes ordering and the acceptance union undefined. Confirm-before-build and the two-attempt stop come last because they are the execution discipline wrapping an already-planned, already-governed pass.

dominance_rules.rule: The verified dependency DAG dominates convenience ordering
dominance_rules.rationale: a convenience order forces rework the moment a hidden dependency surfaces (Feature B's data-not-rendering blocker)
dominance_rules.trigger: a slice or specialist could be run out of dependency order because it looks ready
dominance_rules.action: order by the verified DAG; allow parallelism only where the DAG proves independence

dominance_rules.rationale: a boundary you did not read is a boundary you can cross
dominance_rules.trigger: loading several full specialists is expensive on a multi-domain slice
dominance_rules.action: load every governing specialist in full; flag a partial-load slice out of contract

dominance_rules.rule: Consumption order dominates arbitrary specialist order
dominance_rules.rationale: a downstream authority that runs first reworks the upstream decision it depends on
dominance_rules.action: run schema/meaning before drawing before wording; data-producer before data-consumer

dominance_rules.rationale: polish on the critical path blocks functional slices for cosmetic gain
dominance_rules.trigger: an N.5 polish pass contends with a mainline slice
dominance_rules.action: mainline proceeds; the N.5 pass waits

dominance_rules.rationale: the third re-prompt is the known credit sink and hides an unresolved problem
dominance_rules.action: stop, report honestly, let the owner decide

dominance_rules.rule: The sysloops fence dominates planner's proximity to Slice 8
dominance_rules.rationale: sequencing and verifying Slice 8 is not licence to design its runtime internals
dominance_rules.trigger: a Slice 8 question turns on nightly-loop internals
dominance_rules.action: defer the internal design to sysloops; planner verifies build-vs-spec only

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify every dependency edge before fixing the slice order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ordering the build wrong on an assumed dependency and reworking the sequence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enumerate every domain a slice touches before naming authorities
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a facet shipping ungoverned because its specialist was never named

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the specialist run order by consumption before any of them designs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a downstream authority reworking an upstream decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compose the acceptance union before building, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: declaring done against ad-hoc checks and re-running acceptance later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the sysloops/planner hand-off for Slice 8 before sequencing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a Slice 8 detail falling between planner (sequence/verify) and sysloops (design)

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new specialist is authored that should govern an existing slice type
iteration_protocol.action: re-attach authorities and re-order affected slices by consumption

iteration_protocol.trigger: a feature's true blocker is re-diagnosed from rendering to data (or vice versa)
iteration_protocol.action: re-sequence the data-producer and data-consumer slices

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner reprioritizes a slice (e.g. 'do slice 5 now')
iteration_protocol.action: apply the pull-forward exception and re-derive the next-slice pointer
recompose the affected slices' acceptance tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: the owner redraws the planner/sysloops boundary for Slice 8
iteration_protocol.action: re-state the fence and the hand-off
